name: Java Trivia
description: Oak trees, Duke the mascot, "write once, run anywhere" and some famously surprising one-liners.
question: {prompt}

cards.prompt: Who is known as the father of Java?
cards.fact: Gosling led the small Sun Microsystems team that designed the language in the early 1990s.

cards.prompt: Which company created Java?
cards.fact: Oracle bought Sun, and with it Java, in 2010.

cards.prompt: What was Java's original name?
cards.fact: It was named after an oak tree outside James Gosling's office, then renamed because "Oak" was already trademarked.

cards.prompt: In which year was Java first publicly announced?
cards.fact: Sun announced Java in May 1995; JDK 1.0 followed in January 1996.

cards.prompt: What was Java's famous slogan?
options: There's more than one way to do it
cards.fact: Compiled Java runs on any machine with a Java Virtual Machine, whatever the hardware.

cards.prompt: What is the name of Java's mascot?
cards.fact: Duke, a cheerful black-and-white figure with a red nose, dates back to Sun's early Green Project.

cards.prompt: In which year did Oracle complete its purchase of Sun Microsystems?
cards.fact: The deal made Oracle the steward of Java, MySQL and Solaris.

cards.prompt: How is JavaScript related to Java?
cards.answer: Hardly at all: the name was largely marketing
options: It was also written by James Gosling
cards.fact: Brendan Eich created JavaScript at Netscape in 1995; it was renamed to ride Java's popularity.

cards.prompt: Small Java programs that once ran inside web pages were called…
cards.fact: Browsers dropped the Java plug-in, and the Applet API was deprecated in Java 9.

cards.prompt: JVM stands for…
cards.fact: Many other languages run on the JVM too, including Kotlin, Scala and Clojure.

cards.prompt: The Java compiler turns source code into…
cards.fact: The JVM then interprets the bytecode or compiles it to native code just in time.

cards.prompt: Compiled Java code is stored in files ending in…
cards.fact: Every .class file begins with the magic number 0xCAFEBABE.

cards.prompt: JAR, the format for bundling Java programs, stands for…
cards.fact: A JAR is a ZIP file with a manifest describing its contents.

cards.prompt: How does Java free memory you no longer use?
cards.fact: Modern JVMs ship several collectors, such as G1 and ZGC, tuned for different workloads.

cards.prompt: Which line traditionally starts a Java program?
cards.fact: Java 21 began previewing simpler entry points, but this line is still the classic.

cards.prompt: Calling a method on a null reference throws…
cards.fact: Since Java 15, the error message says by default exactly what was null.

cards.prompt: Which keyword makes a Java variable unchangeable once assigned?
cards.fact: const is actually a reserved word in Java, but it does nothing.

cards.prompt: Which of these is a reserved Java keyword that does nothing?
cards.fact: goto and const are reserved so they can never be used as names.

cards.prompt: Exceptions that a method must either catch or declare with "throws" are called…
cards.fact: IOException is the classic checked exception; most other languages chose not to copy the idea.

cards.prompt: Once created, a Java String is…
cards.fact: Methods like toUpperCase() return a new String rather than changing the old one.

cards.prompt: Which pair are the two most popular Java build tools?
cards.fact: Both download libraries from Maven Central, the main Java package repository.

cards.prompt: Which Java version introduced lambda expressions?
cards.fact: Java 8 (2014) also brought the Streams API.

cards.prompt: Which Java version introduced generics, as in List<String>?
cards.fact: Java 5 (2004) also added enums, annotations and the for-each loop.

cards.prompt: Which Java version added "var" for local variable type inference?
cards.fact: var lets the compiler work out the type: var names = new ArrayList<String>();

cards.prompt: Records (compact data classes) became a standard feature in…
cards.fact: Records previewed in Java 14 and were finalised in Java 16.

cards.prompt: The module system (Project Jigsaw) arrived in…
cards.fact: Project Jigsaw split the huge JDK into modules after years of delays.

cards.prompt: What does this print?
cards.fact: Dividing two ints throws away the remainder.

cards.prompt: What does this print?
cards.fact: Starting from a String, each + joins text, left to right.

cards.prompt: What does this print?
cards.fact: 1 + 2 is added first as numbers, then "3" is joined on.

cards.prompt: What does this print?
cards.fact: A char in arithmetic is its number: 'a' is 97.

cards.prompt: What does this print?
cards.fact: int arithmetic silently wraps around from the largest value to the smallest.

cards.prompt: What does this print?
cards.fact: equals is case-sensitive; equalsIgnoreCase is not.

cards.prompt: What does this print?
cards.fact: Binary floating point cannot store 0.1 exactly; Java shows the tiny error.

cards.prompt: What does this print?
cards.fact: == compares object identity; use equals() to compare the text.

cards.prompt: What does this print?
cards.fact: Java indexes from 0, so charAt(1) is the second character.
